primary_topics: Welcome address by CJP as Foundation President at the reopening of the Manila Cathedral-Basilica after two years of retrofitting and restoration, April 9, 2014

The Cathedral's identity: ecclesia caput et mater omnium ecclesiarum -- head and mother church of all 92 parishes of the Archdiocese of Manila; the cathedra (archbishop's chair) as the symbol of apostolic succession; damaged eight times and rebuilt eight times since its founding in 1581

The distinguished attendance: President Benigno Aquino III and sisters, Senate President Drilon, Mayor Joseph Estrada; plus donors San Miguel Group (Ramon Ang) and Metrobank Group (George Ty, Justa Lee, Antonio Oppen)
Next steps: the 13-bell carillon donated by Bert and Sylvia Lina will be replaced with the new 23-bell set from the Netherlands; air conditioning system still needs a donor

stances.claim: The Cathedral's physical restoration is not yet complete -- the 13-bell carillon is being replaced and the air conditioning still needs a donor. The reopening marks the completion of structural restoration, not the final state; the community's work continues.
stances.rhetorical_move: honest-incompleteness framing: acknowledging what remains undone at a moment of celebration, inviting continued generosity

notable_anecdotes: The Cathedral's eight destructions and eight restorations: founded in 1581, damaged eight times (wars, earthquakes, fires) but rebuilt eight times too -- 'the 8th and latest time' being the two-year retrofitting just completed.

Carillon continuity: the 13 bells donated by Bert and Sylvia Lina will be replaced by them with a completely new set of 23 computerized bells from the Netherlands 'in a few months' -- the carillon upgrade that was in progress at the reopening.

The air conditioning appeal: 'our antiquated air conditioning system will have to be changed as soon as we find a kind donor' -- a public appeal for the next phase of restoration embedded in the reopening welcome.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered April 9, 2014 as the welcome address at the reopening of the Manila Cathedral-Basilica after two years of retrofitting and restoration, this speech by CJP -- as Foundation President, on behalf of Chairman Cardinal Tagle, Vice Chair Ambassador Tita de Villa, Treasurer Marixi Prieto, and Executive Director Monsignor Nestor Cerbo -- opens with a Tagalog greeting to President Benigno Aquino III (with sisters Ballsy, Viel and Kris), Senate President Franklin Drilon and Mila, and Mayor Joseph Estrada and Senadora Loi (CJ Sereno sent regrets, presiding over SC summer sessions in Baguio). Major donors San Miguel Group (Ramon Ang) and Metrobank Group (George Ty, Justa Lee, Antonio Oppen) are acknowledged. Representatives of the 92 parishes of the Archdiocese of Manila (10 per parish) and Caritas (representing the underprivileged, infirm and disabled) are welcomed. CJP delivers a brief theological interlude on 'church': the material structure exists to serve the community of faithful 'called by God to love Him and to love one another in worship, spirit and truth'; the cathedral is the ecclesia caput et mater omnium ecclesiarum, its cathedra (the archbishop's chair) symbolizing apostolic succession and distinguishing it from a parish church or chapel. The Cathedral was founded in 1581, damaged eight times, and rebuilt eight times -- 'the 8th and latest time' being the restoration just completed by contractor DM Consunji and project manager SP Castro. CJP notes that restoration is not yet complete: the 13-bell carillon donated by Bert and Sylvia Lina will be replaced by them with a new 23-bell set from the Netherlands 'in a few months,' and the 'antiquated air conditioning system will have to be changed as soon as we find a kind donor.' The program: audio-visual on the retrofitting; then full lights; Eucharistic Celebration presided by Cardinal Tagle with bishops and pastors; simple repast at Plaza Roma; reception at Arzobispado de Manila for donors and guests.
